subject: microbiology
title: Culture Media II: Enrichment Broths, Biochemical Tests, MALDI-TOF and Blood Culture

steps.tx: **Selenite F broth** enriches Salmonella (and some Shigella) from stool by poisoning coliform rivals with selenite while salmonellae tolerate it, subcultured onto selective plates at 12 to 18 hours before the poison turns on its beneficiaries too. Tetrathionate broth serves the same stool with different chemistry; enrichment timing is a window, not a suggestion.
steps.say: Selenite poisons the rivals first and its beneficiaries later; subculture on schedule.

left.title: Enrichment design
points: Liquid, pathogen favoured over commensals
Selenite F: Salmonella from stool and food
Alkaline peptone water: Vibrio
Subculture window hours, not days

right.title: Enrichment uses
points: Carrier detection (typhoid stool)
Food and water examination
Scanty pathogens in heavy flora
Never a substitute for direct plating

steps.tx: **Transport media** (Stuart, Amies with charcoal, Cary Blair for enterics and vibrios) keep organisms alive without multiplying during journeys from ward, camp or home, buffered and reduced so fastidious Neisseria and anaerobes survive hours. Viral transport medium and anaerobic transport systems are its siblings; a dry swab in a sterile tube is its negation.
steps.say: Transport media promise survival without growth; distance decides which promise a specimen needs.

left.title: Transport roster
points: Stuart and Amies charcoal: general swabs
Cary Blair: stool enterics and Vibrio
Viral transport medium: swabs for NAAT
Anaerobic transport: oxygen excluded

right.title: Specimen transport rules
points: Urine and CSF immediate, never refrigerated CSF for bacteria
Blood cultures at room temperature, loaded fast
Sputum and stool within hours, refrigerate if delayed (not CSF)
Labelled biohazard sealed packaging

steps.tx: The **catalase test** drops hydrogen peroxide on a colony and reads bubbles (staphylococci positive, streptococci negative) within seconds, while the **oxidase test** (tetramethyl p phenylenediamine turning purple) names Neisseria, Pseudomonas, Vibrio and Campylobacter. Two reagent spots sort the gram positive cocci and gram negative worlds before any panel is inoculated, provided blood agar carryover does not fake catalase.
steps.say: Bubbles split staphylococci from streptococci; purple names the oxidase positive gram negatives.

left.title: Catalase logic
points: Positive: staphylococci, most bacilli
Negative: streptococci and enterococci
Avoid blood agar carryover (red cell catalase)
Anaerobes often negative by oxygen logic

right.title: Oxidase logic
points: Positive: Neisseria, Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Pasteurella
Negative: Enterobacterales family wide
Read within 30 seconds, iron loops falsify
Cytochrome c oxidase is the target

steps.tx: **IMViC** (indole, methyl red, Voges Proskauer, citrate) sorts enteric genera by metabolic votes: E coli classic plus plus minus minus, Klebsiella and Enterobacter the mirror minus minus plus plus, with indole from tryptophan (Kovac red ring), MR from stable acid, VP from acetoin, and citrate as sole carbon. Panels automated the questions, not the logic.
steps.say: Indole, MR, VP, citrate: four metabolic votes separate coli from Klebsiella.

left.title: IMViC patterns
points: E coli: + + - -
Klebsiella and Enterobacter: - - + +
Citrate positive: Salmonella and Citrobacter mostly
Indole positive: E coli, Vibrio cholerae (cholera red)

right.title: Bench companions
points: TSI: sugars, gas and H2S in one slant
Urease: Proteus rapid, Klebsiella slower
Motility at 25 versus 37 (Listeria, Yersinia)
API and VITEK galleries miniaturise panels

steps.tx: **MALDI TOF** mass spectrometry identifies colonies in minutes by protein fingerprint (mostly ribosomal proteins) matched against libraries, collapsing days of biochemistry for most bacteria and yeasts, failing gracefully where libraries thin (mycobacteria need extraction, closely related Shigella and E coli blur), and increasingly reading resistance markers. Culture's clock changed; morphology and panels remain its referees.
steps.say: A protein fingerprint names colonies in minutes; the library decides what names exist.

nodes.label: Library match reports identification and score

steps.tx: **Automated blood culture** (BACTEC, BacT ALERT) incubates bottles with growth atmosphere, sensing carbon dioxide colorimetrically or fluorescently around the clock, flagging positive in hours to days (most pathogens within 48 hours), subcultured and Gram stained immediately at the flag. Paired aerobic and anaerobic bottles, adequate volume (the strongest yield variable) and skin antisepsis decide its truth before machinery helps.
steps.say: Blood volume and skin prep decide blood culture truth; the machine only watches patiently.

left.title: Yield variables
points: Volume: 20 to 30 ml per adult set split bottles
Two sets from separate sites before antibiotics
Skin antisepsis and sterile draw
Paediatric single bottle weight guided

right.title: Interpretation
points: Time to positivity hints organism and load
One of four bottles coagulase negative staph: suspect contaminant
Continuous monitoring 5 days standard
Positive Gram stain telephoned as critical result

steps.tx: **Automated blood culture** systems such as BACTEC and BacT ALERT incubate bottles and watch for carbon dioxide by colour or fluorescence around the clock. A positive flag can come in hours, and most pathogens declare within 48 hours. The flagged bottle is Gram stained and subcultured immediately. Machinery does not rescue a poor draw. Paired aerobic and anaerobic bottles, enough blood volume, which is the strongest predictor of yield, and skin antisepsis decide whether a positive result is true infection. Those choices are made before the incubator starts its watch.
steps.say: BACTEC and BacT ALERT watch blood culture bottles continuously for carbon dioxide and often flag growth within 48 hours. A flagged bottle is Gram stained and subcultured at once. Volume of blood and skin preparation decide the truth of the result. The machine only keeps watch.

vis.alt: Automated blood culture bottles are loaded into a continuously monitored incubator that senses carbon dioxide from growing organisms.
vis.caption: Aerobic and anaerobic bottles sit in an automated incubator that flags rising carbon dioxide so the positive bottle can be Gram stained at once. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Specimen quality** precedes all instruments (the morphology lesson's rule serialised): sputum screened for squamous contamination, urine midstream with colony counts interpreted by collection method, stool cultured for defined pathogens not flora, CSF rushed warm, swabs rejected for anaerobic requests and dry sites. Laboratories that publish rejection criteria protect identification machinery from garbage elegantly labelled.
steps.say: Reject bad specimens kindly and in writing; instruments cannot redeem them.

left.title: Quality gates
points: Sputum Gram screen before culture
Urine counts interpreted by collection route
Wounds: tissue or aspirate over swabs
CSF priority transport, cell count paired

right.title: Collection timing
points: Before antibiotics where safe
Blood cultures before fever spike myth discarded
Paired serology needs acute sample saved
Repeat sampling for intermittent shedders

steps.tx: **Automated identification and susceptibility** platforms (VITEK, Phoenix, MicroScan) combine biochemical galleries with turbidimetric antibiotic dilutions into same day answers, while disc diffusion and gradient strips remain referees for difficult pairs. The identification pipeline now runs colony to MALDI name to automated MIC within a working day for routine organisms, rewiring empirical therapy's second day.
steps.say: Name by spectrum, susceptibility by machine, therapy revised by evening: the modern bench day.

left.title: Automated platforms
points: Biochemical ID galleries inoculated from colonies
MIC by turbidimetric dilution series
Expert rules flag implausible phenotypes
LIS interfaces report to stewardship

right.title: Manual referees
points: Disc diffusion for confirmation niches
Gradient strips for single drug MICs
Phenotypic confirmatory tests (ESBL, carbapenemase)
Reference laboratory for the implausible
